Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.desktop2d

Class ShortcutMap

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.desktop2d.ShortcutMap
public final class ShortcutMap extends Object
The 2D desktop's global keyboard-shortcut table: a mapping from a KeyStroke (parsed from its "control alt T" string form) to an action id.

This is pure lookup with no AWT event plumbing, so the default bindings and the parse/resolve rules are unit-testable headless. Shortcuts turns a resolved action id into a call on the desktop, and Desktop2D installs the KeyEventDispatcher that feeds strokes in.

The window switcher's Alt+` binding is deliberately not in this map, so the dispatcher never claims it and the switcher keeps working.

  • Constructor Details

    • ShortcutMap

      public ShortcutMap(Map<String,String> specToAction)
      Builds a map from specToAction, a table of keystroke-spec string to action id. Unparseable specs and null/blank actions are skipped, so a bad custom entry can never break the whole table.

  • Method Details

    • defaults

      public static ShortcutMap defaults()
      The map carrying the default bindings.

    • defaultBindings

      public static Map<String,String> defaultBindings()
      The default keystroke-spec → action table. The combos are chosen to reach an ordinary application window: the host window manager (GNOME/Mutter, Xwayland) grabs Super+key and Ctrl+Alt+arrow before the JVM sees them, so those are avoided here (and reserved for workspace switching later).

    • mergeBindings

      public static Map<String,String> mergeBindings(Map<String,String> customActionToSpec)
      Overlays customActionToSpec (an action -> keystroke-spec table, as decoded from DesktopConfig.getCustomShortcuts()) onto defaultBindings(): any default binding whose action is overridden is dropped, then each custom action -> spec is added. The result is a spec -> action table ready for ShortcutMap(Map). Pure so it can be unit-tested headless; null/blank custom actions or specs are ignored, so a bad override can never remove a default without replacing it.
